concepts.def: IBDP DT uses analysing, designing, planning, creating, evaluating; iterative loops repeat as understanding develops.
Identifies user needs through observation, interviews and PMI charts; benchmarks against existing solutions.
Quantitative and qualitative criteria covering function, ergonomics, aesthetics, materials, cost, sustainability; agreed before design.
Brainstorming, SCAMPER, mood boards and morphological charts produce divergent ideas; convergence selects strongest concept.
Low-fidelity (paper, foam, cardboard) progresses through mid-fidelity (3D-printed) to high-fidelity working models; feedback drives refinement.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Classic Design — a core area of Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Classic Design brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Classic Design.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Whose 2005 Double Diamond models the design process?
options: IDEO
UK Design Council
Stanford d.school
Frog Design

mcqs.q: Which technique systematically alters product attributes?
options: SCAMPER
TRIZ
PMI
SWOT

mcqs.q: What does 'Rethink' mean in the 6 Rs?
options: Trying a design again if it does not work first time.
Thermoplastics are cheaper, so it is worth recycling them.
Thinking about marketing the product.
Questioning whether a product is necessary or could be designed differently for sustainability.

mcqs.q: Why can thermoplastics be recycled but thermosets cannot?
options: Thermoplastics soften when heated and can be remoulded; thermosets have cross-links that lock the shape permanently.
Thinking about marketing the product.
Thermosets are too dangerous to recycle.
Thermoplastics are cheaper, so it is worth recycling them.

mcqs.q: If voltage is doubled and resistance is unchanged, what happens to the current?
options: Current halves.
Current stays the same.
Current doubles (V = IR, so I = V/R).
Thinking about marketing the product.
